evals.prompt: Write a Go HTTP handler that accepts a JSON body with user registration data (name, email, password), validates the input, stores it in a map, and returns a JSON response. Include the struct definitions and a main function.
evals.expected_output: Code should follow all Go best practices: proper error handling with wrapping, interface compliance check, no naked parameters, proper struct tags, guard clauses, proper naming, etc.

Should produce a priority-categorized audit table finding at least: ignored errors (C01), use of interface{}/any (C07), panic in handler (C06), fire-and-forget goroutine (C04), goroutine in init (H13), missing json tags (H08), GetUser naming (M13), import ordering (M01), unnecessary init (H09), and missing defer (H04).

evals.prompt: I need a generic cache implementation in Go with TTL support. It should work with any key/value types. Include methods for Get, Set, Delete, and a background cleanup goroutine for expired entries.
evals.expected_output: Should use generics appropriately (comparable constraint for keys, any for values), proper goroutine lifecycle management with stop channel, mutex protection, time.Duration for TTL, no interface{}, proper error handling.
